## Problem statement

The refactor skill filed an `E741` ("ambiguous variable name: `l`") finding at
line 4756 of `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py`
and injected a `REFACTOR-LP-0MVDFQC2X005S7WE` marker. Investigation shows the
finding is a **false positive**: no committed revision of the file has ever
contained an `l` identifier, and `ruff check` on the current file passes.

## Users

- **Maintainers of the proxy-usage-analysis skill** — need a worklog that does
  not carry phantom technical debt.
- **The refactor skill / future lint sweeps** — need accurate detection; stale
  markers suppress future findings for the same smell type in this file.

User stories:

- As a maintainer, I want the worklog to reflect real defects so triage time is
  not spent re-verifying already-clean code.
- As an agent running `/skill:refactor`, I want a stale `REFACTOR` marker to be
  removed once its smell no longer exists, so the marker does not mask new
  findings.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `ruff check --select E741 .pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py` reports no findings.
- [ ] An AST scan (or equivalent) confirms no `Name`/`arg` identifier equal to `l` (or the other E741 names `O`/`I`) exists in the file.
- [ ] The work item's disposition is recorded in a comment: either **closed as resolved-in-parent** (smell fixed before parent commit `c0f3625f`, no code change) or the stale `REFACTOR-LP-0MVDFQC2X005S7WE` marker block is removed from the file.
- [ ] Testing/validation criterion: the verification commands above are documented in the work item so a reviewer can reproduce the conclusion.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The finding references a **deleted worktree path**
  (`.worklog/worktrees/wl-LP-0MVC144KS001PDR4-surface-attribution-in-reporting-py/`);
  the authoritative file is the main checkout copy.
- `AGENTS.md` repository boundaries: `.pi/` must not be edited unless
  explicitly instructed — removing the marker requires explicit authorisation.
- The repo already carries other stale `REFACTOR` markers (e.g.
  `LP-0MTHLGVPO004DZ56` in the same file, `LP-0MTGDB3D9007TWHA`,
  `LP-0MVB0THT7000KT0G`); a one-off removal would be inconsistent without the
  systemic fix.

## Existing state

- Current HEAD file: 5,023 lines; line 4756 is the docstring
  `"""LP-0MVC144KS001PDR4 — attribution surfaces in the report."""` — a docstring,
  not a variable.
- Every committed revision (40 commits touching the file) checked: zero
  standalone `l` identifiers. `git log -S "for l in"` returns nothing.
- `ruff check` on the file: **All checks passed!**
- AST scan for `Name`/`arg` in `{l, O, I}`: **NONE**.
- The parent item `LP-0MVC144KS001PDR4` ("Surface attribution in reporting.py")
  is `completed`/`done`; its commit `c0f3625f` is the one that both injected the
  marker and (evidently) landed the fixed file — so the smell was resolved in
  the same session, before commit.

## Desired change

Minimal: record the false-positive/resolved-in-parent disposition and close the
item. Optional (requires explicit authorisation under the `.pi/` boundary
rule): delete the six-line `REFACTOR-LP-0MVDFQC2X005S7WE` marker block so the
`formatting` smell type is no longer suppressed for this file.

Systemic follow-up (out of scope, filed as `discovered-from`): the refactor
skill should remove a `REFACTOR` marker when its work item is closed — it
currently only injects (`comment_injection.py` has no removal path), so stale
markers accumulate repo-wide.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py` — lines 1–6 hold the stale `REFACTOR-LP-0MVDFQC2X005S7WE` marker block (optional removal).
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/fixtures.py` — fixtures used by the file; no change expected.
- `.ruff.toml` — confirms `E` (incl. `E741`) is selected and not ignored; no change expected.

## Related work

- `LP-0MVC144KS001PDR4` — Surface attribution in reporting.py (parent session that injected the marker; completed).
- `LP-0MTHLGVPO004DZ56` — Refactor: unused variable `schedule`, same file/marker mechanism (completed; marker still present).
- `LP-0MU1I7T37001CV4O` — ruff I001 candidate false positive at another file (closed as duplicate of an already-fixed parent finding; disposition precedent).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the `l` variable existed only in the pre-commit worktree state
  and was fixed before `c0f3625f`; the worktree is deleted, so this cannot be

- **Risk (scope creep):** "also clean up every stale REFACTOR marker" — record

- **Risk:** removing the marker alone does not fix the systemic leak; without

- **Risk:** misclassifying a real finding as false positive. Mitigated by the
  reproducible AST + ruff checks in the ACs.

- Q: "Is this E741 finding real, or a false positive?" — Answer (Map, evidence-based): **False positive.** No committed revision contains an `l` identifier; `ruff check` passes; AST scan finds no `l`/`O`/`I` names. Evidence path: `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py:4756`.
- Q: "Should the stale `REFACTOR` marker be removed as part of this item?" — Answer: **OPEN QUESTION for the producer.** Recommended: close as resolved-in-parent without touching `.pi/` (respects the repository-boundaries rule); file a separate `discovered-from` item for the systemic marker-removal gap. # Goal (user story)

As a proxy operator, I want a mechanism to restrict which clients may claim high (or any non-default) request priority, so the priority-routing feature cannot be defeated by every client marking every request `X-Priority: high`.

## Background

The priority-routing epic (LP-0MVDT94F0003VHUA) ships v1 with **no trust gate** (decision d from intake): the header is honoured from any reachable client. This item tracks the hardening follow-up.

## Acceptance Criteria (draft)

- A configurable gate restricts who may request priority above `medium` (e.g. trusted-source allowlist of localhost/subnets, shared-secret header, or per-client capability map).
- Unauthorised high-priority claims are silently downgraded to `medium` (no error, no DoS by 4xx) and logged.
- Choice of gate mechanism documented in the epic's appendix; gate is off by default until operator opts in.
- All related documentation updated and full project test suite passes.

# Limiter skip log prints an impossible ratio when the reserve is in use

discovered-from:LP-0MVDUN5CY009VD20

## Problem

`SlidingWindowRateLimiter.check_and_increment()` logs the rejection ratio as
`len(window)/max_rpm`, but with the free-tier reserve
(`LP-0MVDUN5CY009VD20`) the per-caller cap can be lower than the number of
entries already in the window, producing log lines that look like a bug:

```
WARNING - Rate limit exceeded for munitoai-free: 10/7 requests in 60s window
WARNING - Provider budget exhausted: skipping provider=munitoai-free limit=7 reserve=3 ...
```

The `10` is the count in the window (including slots taken by in-progress
sessions), the `7` is the cap applied to this new-session request. Operators and
log analyses read `10/7` as an arithmetic error.

## Desired change

Make the message self-describing, e.g.:

```
Rate limit exceeded for munitoai-free: window=10 cap=7 (reserve in use) requests in 60s window
```

Keep the emitted fields parseable (stable `key=value` tokens) so the
proxy-usage / budget-effectiveness analyses can extract `window=` and `cap=`
instead of inferring them from provider config.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The rejection log line names both the in-window count and the cap applied to
  the rejected request, with no value that can read as `count/cap` confusion.
- A unit test asserts the emitted message contains `window=`, `cap=` and the
  correct numbers for (a) a plain over-limit rejection and (b) a
  reserve-limited rejection (cap < window count).
- No behaviour change: only the message text (and any consumed parse) changes;
  full project test suite passes.
- Stale references quoting the old `N/M requests in Ns window` wording are
  updated to the new format (see Affected references).

## Implementation notes

- The limiter only knows the cap it was handed (`effective_limit`); it does not
  know *why* that cap is below the configured `rate_limit_rpm`. A
  `(reserve in use)` annotation therefore requires the caller
  (`proxy/provider_budget.py`) to pass context, and is optional — the required,
  parseable fields are `window=` and `cap=`.
- If extra context is passed, prefer a stable token over prose so the
  `key=value` convention used by the companion `Provider budget exhausted`
  line is preserved (e.g. `cap=7 reserve=3`, not `(reserve in use)`).
- Test-first: add the message assertions to `proxy/tests/test_rate_limiter.py`
  (plain over-limit case and `cap < window` case) before changing the format
  string.

## Affected references

- `proxy/proxy/rate_limiter.py` — the format string and `logger.warning` call.
- `proxy/tests/test_rate_limiter.py` — unit tests asserting the message fields.
- `proxy/tests/test_chain_hold_budget_window.py` — comment quoting the old
  `13/11 requests in 60s window` wording.
- `proxy/docs/remote-fallback-timeout-budget.md` — same quoted wording.

**Key Files:**
- `proxy/proxy/rate_limiter.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_rate_limiter.py`
- `proxy/docs/remote-fallback-timeout-budget.md`

# Consolidate and document the provider fallback-chain configuration model

discovered-from:LP-0MVDVK5TM004TQQV

## Goal (user story)

As the proxy operator, I want **one** authoritative description of the provider
fallback model — every knob that shapes a chain, the layer it applies at
(provider entry / model / server), and the order those layers win in — so I can
answer "how do I control X for model Y?" without reading `provider.py`, and so
new controls (e.g. per-model budget knobs, `LP-0MVDVK5TM004TQQV`) slot into a
documented contract instead of inventing a new shape.

Low priority: documentation/consolidation only, no behaviour change.

## Current state (fragmented)

Fallback behaviour is described in five places that have drifted apart:
`proxy/config.yaml` header comments, `proxy/README.md`, `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md`,
`proxy/docs/routing.md` and inline code comments in `proxy/proxy/provider.py` /
`provider_budget.py`. The knobs themselves are spread across three layers with
no single statement of precedence:

| Layer | Examples | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Provider entry | `rate_limit_rpm`, `available_times`, `endpoint`, `api_key_env`, `forward_session_headers`, `api`, `system_prompt`, `budget` (proposed) | per-entry, order defines chain position |
| Model (`models.<name>`) | `providers` list order, `aliases`, `system_prompt`, `budget` (proposed) | one model key → one chain, shared by all aliases |
| Server (`server.*`) | `provider_cooldown_seconds`, `sibling_fallback_*`, `chain_hold_*`, `upstream_*`, `provider_rate_limit_*`, `provider_affinity_ttl_seconds`, `max_retry_after_seconds` | global; some are inherited-only across mode overlays |
| Mode overlay | `config-fast.yaml`, `config-cheap.yaml` | lists replace wholesale; other values replace; only diffs declared |
| Runtime | cooldowns, usage-limit quarantine, stall circuit breaker, affinity records, budget windows | in-memory + `proxy/provider-state.json` |

Cross-cutting semantics that are easy to get wrong and belong in one place:
failure-domain grouping (shared endpoint+model), per-account vs per-endpoint
exclusion, time windows (`available_times`), the free-tier budget gate
(`LP-0MVDQ1GMO00801PL`, `LP-0MVDUN5CY009VD20`) including the reserve and
affinity, chain-hold retry cycles, sibling-fallback circuit breaker,
mode grandfathering, and which of these reset on proxy restart (in-memory vs
persisted).

## Desired change

1. A single reference document (e.g. `proxy/docs/provider-fallback-model.md`)
   covering: chain resolution order, every knob with its layer + default +
   precedence, the failure/cooldown/quarantine taxonomies, quota/budget gating,
   mode overlays and grandfathering, and what is persisted vs in-memory.
2. `proxy/README.md` and `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md` link to it instead of duplicating
   the detail (keep short, task-focused sections there).
3. A short "inconsistencies / gaps" section recording anything found while
   writing it (knobs only available globally, provider lists duplicated in the
   fast overlay, budget gating only on one entry, etc.) — recorded as
   `discovered-from` work items rather than fixed here.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `proxy/docs/provider-fallback-model.md` exists and states, for every
   fallback-related knob: name, layer, default, precedence, and the behaviour it
   controls — verified against the code paths that read it (no invented values).
2. A precedence table covers entry > model (where applicable) > server >
   built-in default, including the mode-overlay merge rule (lists replace,
   scalars replace, dicts merge) and the `BASE_ONLY_SERVER_KEYS` inheritance
   contract.
3. The persistence section distinguishes state that survives a restart
   (`provider-state.json`, grandfathered bindings) from in-memory state
   (cooldowns, stall breaker, affinity, budget windows).
4. `proxy/README.md` and `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md` link to the new document and no
   longer contradict it.
5. Every inconsistency found is either fixed by a linked `discovered-from` item
   or explicitly recorded as accepted.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments where a pointer to the new document replaces duplicated prose.
7. Full project test suite passes (documentation-only change must not perturb
   behaviour).

## Constraints

- Documentation/analysis only: no behaviour, config-value or code-path changes in
  this item.
- Do not duplicate the new budget-gate material — reference
  `LP-0MVDQ1GMO00801PL` / `LP-0MVDUN5CY009VD20` and the per-model controls item
  (`LP-0MVDVK5TM004TQQV`) rather than restating their designs.
- UK English, Markdown, no secrets (reference API keys by env-var name only).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/docs/provider-fallback-model.md` — new reference document.
- `proxy/README.md`, `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md`, `proxy/docs/routing.md` — link + trim
  duplicated material.
- `proxy/config.yaml` — header comments point at the document.
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py`, `proxy/proxy/provider_budget.py` — verify claims;
  replace duplicated comments with pointers only where clearly redundant.

## Related work

- `LP-0MVDVK5TM004TQQV` — per-model budget knobs (the contract this document
  should describe once it lands).
- `LP-0MVDQ1GMO00801PL`, `LP-0MVDUN5CY009VD20` — the free-tier budget gate,
  reserve and wait cap.
- `LP-0MVDVJYN5001BMG4` — whether `rate_limit_rpm` should be raised.
- `LP-0MVDNP36J006430L` — header-derived budgeting.
- `LP-0MVDQKF4F008LGS6` — free tier restricted to cheap mode.

## Problem statement

Four offline analysis/benchmark scripts still hard-code the **retired fast/cheap
mode-profile** routing constants (warm clamps 83285 / 100000, cheap cold 42000,
breach caps 83285 / 61440, slot pools 3 / 2). Since LP-0MVHSET0A008VU95 the live
single unified profile resolves to `warm=120000`, `cold=38000`, `slots=2`,
physical clamp `126976`, and since LP-0MVDT94F0003VHUA there is no mode axis at
all — so new `routing_check` logs (`warm_threshold=120000`) fall into no known
bucket and every per-mode cap report is meaningless.

## Users

- **Proxy operator / analyst (Richard)** — runs these scripts over proxy logs to size
  compaction, hard caps and slot geometry. Needs bucket and breach numbers that
  reflect the config actually in force, and that stay reproducible over historical
  log windows.

### Example user stories

- As an analyst, I can run `analyze_context_distribution.py` over the last 7 days and
  get session buckets and breach counts for the **current** warm cap (120000) without
  editing constants first.
- As an analyst, re-running the script over the 2026-08-24..26 window still produces
  its historical (`83285` / `100000`) buckets, so old evaluations remain reproducible.
- As an analyst, `evaluate_hard_routing_cap.py` classifies prefills against the same
  thresholds the router uses (`cold 38000`, `warm 120000`, clamp `126976`, 2 slots),
  so its "above cap" counts match live behaviour.
- As a maintainer, changing the warm cap in `proxy/config.yaml` never again requires
  an edit-and-hope sweep through analysis scripts.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **No hard-coded routing thresholds in analysis/benchmark tooling.**
   `proxy/scripts/analyze_context_distribution.py`,
   `proxy/scripts/correlate_oversized_sessions.py`,
   `proxy/scripts/run_compaction_experiment.py` and
   `proxy/benchmarks/evaluate_hard_routing_cap.py` derive their cold/warm/breach/slot
   values from `proxy/config.yaml` (or from a single shared pure resolver — see
   Constraint C2). Grep proves it: no literal `83285`, `100000`, `42000`, `61440` or
   `87381` remains as a default in those files.
2. **Current live values are produced, and historical logs still classify.**
   With the shipped config the scripts resolve `cold=38000`, `warm=120000`,
   physical clamp `126976`, `slots=2`; a `routing_check` sample carrying
   `warm_threshold=120000` lands in the current bucket (not `other`), while samples
   from older logs (`83285`, `100000`) still bucket by their **observed**
   `warm_threshold` value rather than collapsing into `other`.
3. **`evaluate_hard_routing_cap.py` MODES matches the live unified profile.**
   The fast/cheap mode split is replaced by (or collapses to) one profile with
   `cold_cache_threshold=38000`, `warm_cache_threshold_config=120000`,
   `session_slot_pool_size=2`, `local_model_ctx_size=262144`,
   `routing_clamp=126976` — or the config-derived equivalents — and
   `proxy/tests/test_evaluate_hard_routing_cap.py` (which currently asserts
   `warm_threshold(fast) == 83285` / `== 100000`) is updated to assert the derived
   values and the new prefill-bucket boundaries.
4. **Tests cover the regression.** Both test modules
   (`proxy/tests/test_analyze_context_distribution.py`,
   `proxy/tests/test_evaluate_hard_routing_cap.py`) assert against a config fixture,
   including a `warm_threshold=120000` case and a legacy `83285`/`100000` case, so a
   future cap change in `config.yaml` cannot silently desynchronise the tooling.
5. **No production behaviour change.** No file under `proxy/proxy/` changes routing
   behaviour (a pure-helper extraction, if taken, must be a behaviour-preserving move
   covered by the existing suite); docstrings/help text that describe the old mode
   profiles are corrected.
6. **Docs updated** — `proxy/docs/context-compaction-eval/README.md`,
   `docs/dev/hard-local-routing-cap-evaluation.md` and any script docstrings that
   quote the retired mode thresholds now describe the unified-profile derivation.
7. **Full project test suite passes** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **C1 — offline only.** None of these scripts is on the production routing path; a
  fix must not touch routing decisions, `provider.py` logic, or `config.yaml` values.
- **C2 — dependency weight.** The analysis scripts are deliberately stdlib-only and
  are imported directly by tests (`import analyze_context_distribution`). Importing
  `proxy.proxy.provider` would drag in `fastapi`/`httpx`; therefore prefer extracting
  the *pure* resolvers (`effective_per_slot_threshold`, warm/cold/slot/ctx getters,
  `effective_large_context_economic_ceiling`) into a stdlib-only module
  (e.g. `proxy/proxy/routing_thresholds.py`) that both `provider.py` and the scripts
  import. If the extraction proves invasive, a script-local `yaml`-based resolution
  that reuses the same formula is acceptable **provided** it is the only copy and is
  test-pinned against the live config — duplicating the formula in three scripts is
  not acceptable (it is how this defect arose).
- **C3 — historical reproducibility.** Aug-2026 evaluation artifacts
  (`proxy/docs/context-compaction-eval/distribution.{json,md}`) were produced with the
  old clamps; re-running over the same window must still yield those buckets.
- **C4 — CLI compatibility.** `--fast-cap` / `--cheap-cap` / `--mode fast|cheap` flags
  may be retired, but any removal must be documented in the docstring/help text and
  should not break the documented invocation examples.
- **C5 — repo boundaries.** No edits to `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/` in this
  item even though it carries mode-aware report logic; that skill already resolves
  per-mode triggers from config (`reporting.py:_mode_trigger`) and is not stale in the
  same way.

## Existing state

Live `proxy/config.yaml` (unified profile, mode overlays removed):

| key | value |
|---|---|
| `local_model_ctx_size` | 262144 |
| `session_slot_pool_size` | 2 |
| `local_large_context_cold_cache_threshold` | 38000 |
| `local_large_context_warm_cache_threshold` | 120000 |
| `local_large_context_economic_ceiling_ratio` | 0.4578 → ceiling 120010, capped to 120000 |
| physical per-slot clamp | `262144 // 2 - 4096` = **126976** |
| effective warm | `min(120000, 126976)` = **120000** (matches logged `warm_threshold=120000`) |

Stale constants found:

| file | symbol | value | live equivalent |
|---|---|---|---|
| `proxy/scripts/analyze_context_distribution.py` | `FAST_WARM_THRESHOLD` | 83285 | 120000 (only profile) |
| " | `CHEAP_WARM_THRESHOLD` | 100000 | — (mode retired) |
| " | `FAST_CAP` | 83285 | 120000 |
| " | `CHEAP_CAP` | 61440 | — (mode retired) |
| `proxy/scripts/correlate_oversized_sessions.py` | `FAST_CAP`, `CHEAP_CAP` | 83285, 61440 | as above |
| `proxy/scripts/run_compaction_experiment.py` | `FAST_WARM_THRESHOLD`, `CHEAP_WARM_THRESHOLD` + `Mode.from_warm_threshold` | 83285, 100000 | 120000 |
| `proxy/benchmarks/evaluate_hard_routing_cap.py` | `MODES["fast"]` | cold 38000, warm 100000, slots 3, clamp 83285 | cold 38000, warm 120000, slots 2, clamp 126976 |
| " | `MODES["cheap"]` | cold 42000, warm 100000, slots 2, clamp 100000 | (collapse to the unified profile) |

Existing single-source-of-truth helpers already in the proxy:
`provider.effective_per_slot_threshold`, `provider.effective_large_context_economic_ceiling`,
`provider.compute_hard_routing_cap` (mode argument retained but the per-mode ratios are
retired), `provider._effective_large_context_thresholds(config) -> (cold, warm)`.

## Desired change

1. Introduce one stdlib-only resolver module (or reuse an existing light one) that
   maps `config.yaml` → `(cold, warm, physical_clamp, slots, ctx_size, hard_cap)`
   using the shipped 3-term warm model, and make `provider.py` import the pure
   functions from it (behaviour-preserving move, no logic change).
2. Point all four scripts at that resolver. Replace the mode-bucket heuristic with
   **observed-value bucketing**: bucket/label each session by the `warm_threshold`
   value in its own log lines (e.g. `warm=120000`, `warm=83285`), and compute breach
   counts against the resolved cap for the *current* config by default, with a
   `--warm-cap`/`--cold-cap` override for historical replay. `warm_threshold=120000`
   must therefore be a first-class bucket, and the `other` fallback only catches
   genuinely unknown values.
3. Collapse `evaluate_hard_routing_cap.MODES` to a single profile derived from config;
   keep the `--mode` flag only if it remains meaningful (otherwise retire it and say so
   in the docstring). Update the two test modules accordingly.
4. Correct every docstring/help string that still describes the fast/cheap mode
   profiles as live.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/proxy/routing_thresholds.py` — New (or equivalent): stdlib-only pure resolvers for effective cold/warm/clamp/slots from a config dict, extracted from `provider.py`.
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — Import the pure resolvers from the new module (behaviour-preserving; no logic change).
- `proxy/scripts/analyze_context_distribution.py` — Drop the four hard-coded constants; resolve thresholds from config; replace mode bucketing with observed-`warm_threshold` bucketing; correct the docstring's "Mode classification" section.
- `proxy/scripts/correlate_oversized_sessions.py` — Drop its duplicated `FAST_CAP`/`CHEAP_CAP`; use the shared resolver and the same bucket keys as the analyser.
- `proxy/scripts/run_compaction_experiment.py` — Drop `FAST_WARM_THRESHOLD`/`CHEAP_WARM_THRESHOLD` and the `Mode.from_warm_threshold` table.
- `proxy/benchmarks/evaluate_hard_routing_cap.py` — Replace `MODES` fast/cheap entries with the single config-derived profile (`cold 38000`, `warm 120000`, slots 2, clamp 126976).

# Goal (bug)

As an operator, I want a change to `models.ini` or `start-llama.sh` (model launch arguments: `ubatch-size`, `batch-size`, `ctx-size`, cache types, …) to force a llama-server restart on `start-proxy.sh --restart`, so a config edit is never silently left inactive.

## Evidence (2026-10-22, LP-0MVIQ0FSX006HQOS)

Setting `ubatch-size = 2048` in `models.ini` [Qwen3] and `UBATCH_SIZE=2048` / `LLAMA_UBATCH_SIZE:=2048` in `start-llama.sh`, then running `scripts/start-proxy.sh --restart`, left llama-server running with `--ubatch-size 1024`. Cause: the preserve decision hashes only the merged `config.yaml`

```
_restart_sha=$(merged_config_sha256(config.yaml, <overlay>))
# compared with .llama_server_signature.json config_sha256
if [ "$_sig_sha" = "$_restart_sha" ]; then KEEP_LLAMA=1; fi
```

`models.ini` and `start-llama.sh` are the actual launch-argument sources (the startup log even prints `BATCH_SIZE=…`), but they are not part of the signature, so any edit to them is invisible to the restart decision.

Workaround used at the time: delete `proxy/.llama_server_signature.json` to force `KEEP_LLAMA=0`. That is undocumented and easy to get wrong (the file lives under `proxy/`, not the repo root, although the script computes `REPO_ROOT` as the parent of `proxy/`).

## Proposed change

1. Include the model-launch inputs in the restart signature: hash `models.ini` and `start-llama.sh` (and any other launch-argument source the launch path reads, e.g. the ini selected by `$LLAMA_MODELS_PRESET` when set) alongside the merged config.
2. Surface the reason in the restart output, e.g. `Restarting llama-server: models.ini changed since last start`, next to the existing preserve message.
3. Document the forced-restart escape hatch (removing `proxy/.llama_server_signature.json`, and a `--force-llama-server` flag if one is added) in the start-proxy skill and `proxy/README.md`.
4. Fail-safe direction: a signature file written before this change carries no launch-input hashes, so the first `--restart` after upgrading sees a mismatch and restarts llama-server once — same fail-safe precedent as LP-0MUJRVYQH002IEHW (a wrong preserve is worse than one cold start).
5. One shared helper: the signature is **written** by `proxy/proxy/lifecycle.py` (`_write_llama_server_signature` → `_config_file_sha256`) and **read** by both `proxy/scripts/start-proxy.sh` (restart gate) and `lifecycle._try_adopt_running_llama_server` (adoption gate). All three must derive the same extended value, so the extension belongs in the shared `proxy/proxy/config_merge.py` helper surface, not duplicated in shell.

## Key Files

- `proxy/scripts/start-proxy.sh` — restart gate (`KEEP_LLAMA` decision, `_sig_sha` vs `_restart_sha`), `--keep-llama-server` flag parsing; signature file resolved as `$REPO_ROOT/.llama_server_signature.json` where `REPO_ROOT` is `proxy/`.
- `proxy/proxy/lifecycle.py` — write path `_config_file_sha256()` / `_write_llama_server_signature()` (~lines 65–115); adoption gate `_try_adopt_running_llama_server()` (LP-0MUPIIDPW009RMLB, ~line 145); `_llama_server_signature_path()`.
- `proxy/proxy/config_merge.py` — home of the shared `merged_config_sha256()` helper; extend/add the launch-input signature helper here so shell and Python agree byte-for-byte, with a JSON/CLI entry point the shell can call.
- `start-llama.sh` — launch-argument source: reads `models.ini` (`ngl`, per-model `ctx-size`), builds `--batch-size` / `--ubatch-size` / `--ctx-size` / cache flags; prints `BATCH_SIZE=…` at startup.
- `models.ini` — per-model and `[global]` launch arguments (`ngl`, `ctx-size`, `ubatch-size`, …).
- `tests/test_start_proxy_mode.sh` — bash harness with stubbed `pkill` and existing unchanged / base-only / overlay-only restart tests; natural home for the models.ini and start-llama.sh restart tests.
- `proxy/tests/test_restart_lifecycle.py` — signature write/read and adoption hash-mismatch tests.
- `proxy/tests/test_config_merge.py` — shared-hash helper tests.
- `proxy/README.md` — restart-signature section (~line 1290) and `start-proxy.sh` CLI flags table (~line 1855).
- `.pi/skills/start-proxy/SKILL.md` — operator-facing restart guidance. AC5 explicitly authorises this edit; it is agent-framework infrastructure and out of bounds under normal repository boundaries.

## Implementation notes (test-first)

1. **Tests first.** Extend `tests/test_start_proxy_mode.sh` with: a `models.ini` value change restarts, a `models.ini` comment-only change restarts, a `start-llama.sh` change restarts, and an unchanged trio still preserves. Extend `proxy/tests/test_restart_lifecycle.py` and `proxy/tests/test_config_merge.py` with writer-side parity and adoption rejection on a launch-input change.
2. **Shared helper.** Add the extended signature (signature value + per-input hashes) to `proxy/proxy/config_merge.py`, callable both from Python and from the shell gate, so `start-proxy.sh` never reimplements hashing.
3. **Signature payload.** Persist per-input hashes in `proxy/.llama_server_signature.json` (e.g. `launch_inputs: {"models.ini": "<sha>", "start-llama.sh": "<sha>"}`) so the gate can name exactly what changed; keep the existing `config_sha256`/`model`/`parallel`/`router_mode` keys.
4. **Shell gate.** Compute the extended signature in the `--restart` block and, on mismatch, echo e.g. `Restarting llama-server: models.ini changed since last start` (falling back to a generic message when the change cannot be attributed).
5. **Docs.** `proxy/README.md` restart-signature section + CLI flags table, and `.pi/skills/start-proxy/SKILL.md`.

## Verification

- Targeted: `bash tests/test_start_proxy_mode.sh` and `python3 -m pytest proxy/tests/test_restart_lifecycle.py proxy/tests/test_config_merge.py` (single-file/targeted runs are permitted; the full suite goes through `/skill:test`).
- Manual (AC1): edit `models.ini`, run `proxy/scripts/start-proxy.sh --restart`, confirm the restart output names the changed input and the new process argv / `BATCH_SIZE=` line reflects the edit.
- Full suite green via `/skill:test` before commit.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: Editing `models.ini` (a comment-only change and a value change, tested separately) followed by `start-proxy.sh --restart` restarts llama-server (test or documented manual verification with the observed argv).
- AC2: Editing `start-llama.sh` likewise restarts llama-server.
- AC3: An unchanged config/models.ini/start-llama.sh trio still preserves the warm llama-server (no regression to LP-0MUCEFCL6001ZXYN).
- AC4: The restart output captured in the startup log names which launch input changed, e.g. `Restarting llama-server: models.ini changed since last start`.
- AC5: The forced-restart path is documented in `.pi/skills/start-proxy/SKILL.md` and `proxy/README.md` (minimum: removing `proxy/.llama_server_signature.json`; documenting a `--force-llama-server` flag instead is acceptable if one is added).
- AC6: The Python write path (`lifecycle._config_file_sha256` / signature writer) and the adoption gate (`_try_adopt_running_llama_server`) derive the same extended signature as the shell restart gate — one shared helper, parity covered by a test — so an unchanged trio is still preserved on every path and an edited launch input is rejected on every path.
- AC7: Full test suite green; commit + hash recorded.

## Assumptions / out of scope

- Launch inputs are hashed as raw file bytes, so a comment-only `models.ini` edit also forces a restart (AC1 requires this explicitly).
- In-scope launch inputs are the resolved models ini (repo-root `models.ini`, or the ini named by `$LLAMA_MODELS_PRESET` when set) and the resolved launch script (repo-root `start-llama.sh`, or `server.llama_start_script` when configured). The container launch path (`scripts/podman_start_llama.sh`) does not read `models.ini` and is out of scope.
- No child decomposition: the effort/risk estimate is Small effort (~12 h recommended, range 9.8–16.5 h) and Medium risk — one vertical slice (shared helper + shell gate + Python writer + tests + docs), so child items would add ceremony without independent deliverables.

## Related work

- LP-0MVIQ0FSX006HQOS — the ubatch A/B where this was hit (reverted; commit c9a49039).
- LP-0MUCEFCL6001ZXYN — the original "preserve the warm llama-server on a proxy-only restart" decision this must not regress.
- LP-0MVAPNC2900145RH — restart-reason plumbing in the same script.
- LP-0MUJRVYQH002IEHW — merged-config (base + overlay) signature; the precedent this change extends.
- LP-0MUPIIDPW009RMLB — the same signature hash on the hot-swap adoption path.

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want a resumed session whose conversation actually continues
a persisted slot snapshot to earn the restored-prefix routing credit, while a
genuinely changed prompt still earns nothing — so the restored-prefix feature
(LP-0MVGD9YXH008O304) is measurable instead of silently dead.

## Why (evidence)

LP-0MVGGPSVM003W35K found zero `cache_state=restored` dispatches in 54.4 h
despite healthy sidecar writing; LP-0MVJXV0MY000O77E AC1 (via its diagnosis
child) names the confirmed failure mode from the instrumented
`slot_ratio_seed outcome=…` counts. This item applies the minimal change that
makes the common resume pattern earn credit while preserving the AC2/AC3
guards of LP-0MVGD9YXH008O304.

## Scope

**In scope:** the confirmed-cause change to the seed guard (and/or the sidecar
TTL) in `proxy/proxy/slot_cache_ratio.py`, evaluated at **both** call sites,
plus the red→green reproducer test and the `routing.md` update. **Out of
scope:** any change not needed for the confirmed cause, re-running the
measurement (sibling item), and any change to the sidecar schema version or
the fail-open behaviour.

## Proposed change

1. **Test-first:** write the unit test reproducing the confirmed pattern in
   `proxy/tests/test_slot_cache_ratio_restore.py` — sidecar saved for a full
   conversation, resumed request arriving with a rebuilt system prompt or a
   front-compacted history (whatever the verdict named). Run it against the
   pre-fix code, capture the failing (red) output in a comment on this item,
   then make it pass with the fix.
2. Implement the smallest fix that credits the reusable prefix and still
   refuses a genuinely changed prompt, e.g. fingerprint the non-system
   messages only, anchor on a stable prompt-prefix hash, credit the
   last-saved overlapping messages, or compare against the last K stored
   fingerprints. Preserve the ratio cap (`min(1.0, cached/estimated) ×
   margin`), the sidecar schema version, and fail-open.
3. Evaluate the same guard change at the **second call site** —
   `provider.expected_cached_ratio()` (~L812) uses `prefix_matches` for the
   in-memory expected-reuse credit. Apply the change consistently there and
   assert a genuinely changed prompt still earns nothing (AC4 of the parent).
4. Re-evaluate the TTL only if the diagnosis proved it binding: either keep
   it, change the default in `ttl_seconds()`, or relax the check per the
   verdict's `age_s` evidence — with the number recorded in this item.
5. Update the restored-prefix warmness section of `proxy/docs/routing.md`
   (~L475–530): the resolved guard, what still earns nothing, the failure
   modes, and the config knobs that affect them.
6. Run the changed-scope test gate through the test skill; record the green
   result in a comment.

## Acceptance criteria

- The reproducer unit test matches the confirmed resume pattern, fails on the pre-fix code (red output captured in a comment), and passes after the fix.
- No regression on AC2/AC3 of LP-0MVGD9YXH008O304: a mismatched snapshot earns nothing and the restored ratio stays ≤ measured × safety margin — the existing cap and prefix tests (`TestRatioCap`, `test_changed_system_prompt_does_not_match`, `test_front_truncated_history_does_not_match`) stay green.

# Re-measure restored vs cold over ≥24 h after the fix

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want a ≥24 h post-fix window that proves the restored-prefix
credit actually fires (`cache_state=restored` dispatches exist) and that it
pays for itself (seeded dispatches beat cold dispatches in the same context
bucket), so AC3 of LP-0MVJXV0MY000O77E is answered with real numbers.

## Why (evidence)

The baseline (LP-0MVGGPSVM003W35K) recorded **0** `cache_state=restored`
dispatches in 54.4 h and **0** `slot_ratio_restored` seeds — so the fix item's
green test gate is not enough; the field measurement is the acceptance test.
The pre-fix local-prefill improvement in that window was caused by other
changes (expected-reuse credit, admission ordering) and must not be used as
evidence for this path (attribution caveat on the parent item).

## Scope

**In scope:** deploying nothing new (the fix item's build), waiting out a
≥24 h window, and producing the before/after comparison with
`scripts/analyse_slot_ratio_restore.py`. **Out of scope:** changing the seed
path again if the window shows zero restored dispatches — that reopens the
diagnosis with the new evidence rather than silently tweaking the guard.

## Proposed change

1. Confirm the fix build (the sibling item's worktree merge) is the deployed
   proxy version, and note the deploy timestamp.
2. Wait out a ≥24 h window (per shared background-job etiquette: launch, do
   other work, then one completion-aware wait). Optionally aggregate the
   `slot_ratio_seed outcome=…` counts for the same window to cross-check the
   seed share.
3. Run `scripts/analyse_slot_ratio_restore.py` over the baseline window and
   the post-fix window (machine-readable `--json` output saved alongside the
   report).
4. State the verdict on LP-0MVJXV0MY000O77E:
   - `cache_state=restored` dispatch count and `slot_ratio_restored` seed
     count (>0 required);
   - restored-vs-cold `dispatch_to_first_byte_ms` p50/p90 with sample counts,
     same context bucket (reuse the bucket table layout from the baseline);
   - sidecar inventory at report time, and the `slot_save`/`slot_restore`
     confound rows.
5. Add the report (a section appended to
   `docs/dev/slot-prefix-warmness-measurement-LP-0MVGGPSVM003W35K.md` or a new
   file under `docs/dev/`) and link it from the parent item.
6. If the window still shows 0 restored dispatches, record the honest result,
   state the outcome counts that explain it (via the diagnosis item's
   aggregation recipe), and file a follow-up — do not claim success.

## Acceptance criteria

- A post-fix window of ≥24 h contains more than zero `cache_state=restored` dispatches and more than zero `slot_ratio_restored` seed events, with the exact counts stated.
- `dispatch_to_first_byte_ms` percentiles (at least p50 and p90) for restored dispatches are stated against cold dispatches **in the same context bucket**, with sample counts for both groups.
- The same window's `slot_ratio_seed outcome=…` counts are aggregated, so the restored share is explainable from the seeding outcomes.
- A written report is added under `docs/dev/` (or appended to the baseline report) with the command line used, and is linked from LP-0MVJXV0MY000O77E.
- If restored dispatches are still zero, the verdict says so honestly, explains the outcome counts, and creates a follow-up item instead of claiming success.

## Risks / notes

- Snapshot-bearing traffic is thin (2,918 gated decisions / 54 h baseline);

# Measure slot save cost: wall time, on-disk size, success rate

Parent: LP-0MVGD9ZKI004ETTE. Measurement 1 of the spike.

## Target outcome

A measured table of `slot save` cost for prompt sizes 38K / 72K / 100K / 124K
tokens: wall-clock time, on-disk snapshot size, bytes per token, and success
rate — including the intermittent ReadTimeout failures, which must be counted,
not retried away.

## Minimal implementation

- Measurement mode in `proxy/benchmarks/slot_save_restore_benchmark.py`
  (`--mode save --sizes 38000,72000,100000,124000 --reps N`).
- Per repetition: unique salted prompt → completion to force a real prefill into
  the slot → `POST /slots/{id}?action=save` → record elapsed, status, on-disk
  `stat().st_size` of the snapshot, plus the llama-server log's own
  `prompt_save: - saving prompt with length N, total state size = X MiB` line for
  cross-validation.
- Derive bytes/token = size / prompt_n and compare with the profile's physical
  KV-per-token expectation from `proxy/benchmarks/kv_memory_table.py`.
- Emit `results/<label>/save.json` + a markdown table with per-size
  p50 / p90 / max save seconds and success rate; failures broken out by
  outcome class (`timeout`, `http_error`, `exception`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Results table covering all four prompt sizes with, per size: n attempts,
  success rate, save wall time p50/p90/max, snapshot size, bytes/token.
- Observed failure rate and failure classes recorded explicitly; if zero failures
  occur the report states the sample size and the window's historical rate
  (`slot_save failed` count) instead of implying saves are reliable.
- The llama-server log's `total state size` agrees with the on-disk size within
  5%, or the discrepancy is reported with an explanation.
- Repeated runs are reproducible: re-running with the same `--sizes`/`--reps`
  produces a new timestamped result directory and does not overwrite prior
  results.
- The run is safe to interrupt and leaves no snapshot it did not record
  (cleanup of its own files listed in the results).

## Constraints

- Save must be issued only when the slot is otherwise idle; concurrent saves are
  serialised by llama-server and would inflate the timing.
- Snapshot files are large (~0.5-0.7 GiB each) — the run must cap total bytes
  written and clean up after itself via `scripts/cleanup-slot-cache.sh`
  semantics, without touching snapshots it did not create.

## Risks

- The `session_slot_skip_when_busy` production gate does not exist in this
  harness path, so saves will be issued under whatever load exists; the run must
  record competing local activity (proxy `local_dispatch_records`) per attempt.

## Key Files

- `proxy/benchmarks/slot_save_restore_benchmark.py`
- `proxy/benchmarks/results/<label>/save.json` (new artifact)
- `scripts/cleanup-slot-cache.sh`
- `docs/slot-persistence-analysis-harness.md` (evidence schema reference)

# Measure restore cost and restore hit-rate (the core spike question)

Parent: LP-0MVGD9ZKI004ETTE. Measurement 2 — this is the load-bearing question:
does a restore actually avoid re-prefill, and how much does it cost?

## Target outcome

For each prompt size (38K / 72K / 100K / 124K), a paired comparison between
(a) a **cold** run — fresh slot, no snapshot, full prefill — and (b) a
**restored** run — save, evict/clear the slot, restore, then replay the same
prompt — reporting time-to-first-token, tokens actually evaluated
(`timings.prompt_n`), tokens reused from cache, and the resulting hit-rate.

## Minimal implementation

- `--mode restore` in the harness: for each size and repetition run the pair
  `cold` then `save → clear slot → restore → replay` and record both rows.
- Hit is derived from tokens, not wall time: `cached_tokens = prompt_total -
  timings.prompt_n`, `cached_ratio = cached_tokens / prompt_total`. A run is a
  **hit** when `cached_ratio >= --hit-threshold` (default 0.9); a run is a
  **miss** when the restore returned OK but `prompt_n` shows a full re-prefill.
  Latency is reported alongside, never used as the primary hit definition.
- Report per size: cold prefill seconds (p50), restored first-byte seconds (p50),
  speed-up factor, hit-rate, and miss/partial-hit distribution.
- Cross-check against the llama-server log (restored-checkpoint lines / full
  re-processing markers) and against `usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens`
  from the completion response, recording any disagreement.
- `results/<label>/restore.json` + markdown table; the JSON must be directly
  consumable by the break-even model in the verdict child.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Paired cold-vs-restored table for all four sizes, n >= 3 per cell, with
  per-size: cold TTFT p50, restored TTFT p50, speed-up, hit-rate, and the
  distribution of `cached_ratio`.
- The hit definition (`cached_ratio >= threshold`) is documented in the results
  output and the doc, and both the token-based and latency-based views are
  reported so the verdict can cite either.
- Partial hits are reported distinctly from full misses (a 40% prefix reuse is
  not a "miss").
- Any disagreement between `timings.prompt_n`, the response
  `cached_tokens`, and the llama-server log markers is reported, not silently
  reconciled.
- The cold baseline for each size is measured in the same run and window as its
  restored pair, so no cross-run drift is attributed to restore.
- Results are reproducible (timestamped result dir; salt recorded so the same
  prompts can be regenerated).

## Constraints

- The restore must be issued into a slot that does not already hold the same
  prefix, otherwise the measurement proves nothing — the harness must clear or
  overwrite the slot between save and restore and assert that it did.

## Risks

- If llama-server refuses to restore a snapshot for a hybrid-attention model, the
  failure will surface as either an explicit non-200 or a silent full re-prefill.
  The harness must distinguish these (this is the difference between "restore is
  broken" and "restore is ignored").

## Key Files

- `proxy/benchmarks/slot_save_restore_benchmark.py`
- `proxy/benchmarks/results/<label>/restore.json` (new artifact)
- `proxy/proxy/session.py` (`_restore_slot_snapshot` semantics)
- `proxy/proxy/slot_cache_ratio.py` (cached-token derivation reference)

# Characterise restored-cache invalidation (hybrid-attention behaviour)

Parent: LP-0MVGD9ZKI004ETTE. Measurement 3.

## Target outcome

Quantified answer to the hypothesis risk in the parent: this build is Qwen3.x
hybrid attention + recurrent/SWA, and llama.cpp already invalidates its own
context checkpoints, so a restored snapshot may be rejected or only partially
usable. Produce a measured invalidation rate by *reuse shape*, plus the tokens
re-processed as a result.

## Minimal implementation

- `--mode invalidation` in the harness, driving four restore shapes per size:
  1. exact replay — same prompt, no extension (best case);
  2. one-turn extension — same prompt + a short follow-up user turn (the real
     session pattern);
  3. prefix drift — same prompt with a modified system-prompt head (should
     always miss, guards against over-crediting);
  4. cold control — no snapshot at all.
- Parse llama-server log markers between requests: `forcing full prompt
  re-processing`, `erased invalidated context checkpoint ... n_swa`,
  `restored context checkpoint`, and `n_past = ... slot.prompt.tokens.size()`.
  Attribute markers to an attempt by slot id + log offset captured immediately
  before and after each request.
- Report per shape: restore-OK rate, full-reprocessing rate, mean/median tokens
  re-processed, and the effective usable prefix (cached tokens on the first
  completion after restore).
- Emit `results/<label>/invalidation.json` + markdown table.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Invalidation table for the four restore shapes at each prompt size, with
  n >= 3 per cell: restore-OK rate, full-reprocessing rate, tokens re-processed
  (median/p90), effective usable prefix fraction.
- Requirement from `AGENTS.md` respected: `forcing full prompt re-processing` is
  reported as *expected hybrid-arch behaviour with a cost*, never as a defect —
  the table quantifies the cost, and the doc says so explicitly.
- The prefix-drift control behaves as expected (near-zero usable prefix); if it
  does not, the recording/attribution method is reported as unproven and the
  numbers are marked non-authoritative rather than published as fact.
- The one-turn-extension shape is measured, because it is the shape that decides
  whether virtual slots help real sessions (which always extend context).
- Log-marker attribution method is documented so another operator can reproduce
  the counts from the raw logs.

## Constraints

# Harness-side virtual-slot prototype: 8 session slots over 2 physical slots

Parent: LP-0MVGD9ZKI004ETTE. Measurement 5 — the end-to-end contention
comparison. **Gated on OPEN QUESTION 2** (recorded on the parent): AC5 of the
spike asks for 8 virtual slots over 2 physical slots, but virtual slots do not
exist and must not be added to production. This child delivers the measurement
as a *harness-side prototype* unless the producer directs otherwise.

## Target outcome

A measured p50/p90 first-byte latency and throughput comparison between
(A) 2 logical sessions on 2 physical slots (today's baseline) and (B) 8 logical
sessions multiplexed onto 2 physical slots by swap-in/swap-out of KV snapshots,
using a synthetic 8-concurrent-session workload.

## Minimal implementation

- `proxy/benchmarks/virtual_slot_prototype.py` (or a `--mode virtual` in the
  harness): an 8-entry session table mapping logical session → physical
  llama-server slot; on dispatch it restores the session's snapshot into a free
  physical slot (evicting the current occupant with a save first), issues the
  completion, then saves the session's snapshot back.
- Workload: 8 concurrent synthetic sessions, each doing K turns with a shared
  prefix and per-turn growth, sized from the spike's four prompt sizes; turn
  gaps chosen to force real evictions.
- Metrics per configuration: TTFT p50/p90, per-session abandon count (requests
  that could not get a physical slot within the configured queue budget — the
  harness's analogue of `fallback_after_queue`), save/restore counts and
  failures, restored-hit rate, and completion count.
- Both configurations run back-to-back in one invocation so drift is shared.
- Emit `results/<label>/contention.json` + markdown table with an explicit
  A/B delta column.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A/B table for N_logical = 2 (baseline) vs N_logical = 8 over 2 physical slots:
  TTFT p50/p90, throughput, abandon count, save/restore counts, hit-rate,
  per-configuration duration.
- The eviction cost is counted, not hidden: for every restore that displaces
  another session, the displaced session's next-turn cold cost is measured and
  reported (this is the "eviction cost it imposes" term the parent requires).
- The run states plainly whether the prototype is a faithful model of a
  production virtual-slot implementation, listing the differences (no proxy
  routing, no dispatch leases, no contention queue) — no implied production
  parity.
- If 8-over-2 cannot complete within a bounded budget (e.g. wall-clock cap), the
  partial result is reported with the completion fraction rather than being
  silently truncated.
- The prototype lives only under `proxy/benchmarks/`; a test/documentation
  assertion confirms no production module is imported for dispatch.

## Constraints

- No production behaviour change (parent AC5).
- Must not starve live sessions: the run requires a quiet window or an explicit
  recorded validity caveat, mirroring
  `docs/slot-count-reevaluation-LP-0MVGCQ3QN009HRE8.md` § `Fidelity caveats`.

## Risks

- Two prior live sweeps failed under concurrent load (600-760 s stalls,
  llama-server health probes unanswered). If the quiet window cannot be obtained,

  so — do not retry the live run indefinitely.

# Intake brief — slot_benchmark: record finish_reason per request

**Headline:** Record each benchmark request's `finish_reason` in `slot_<N>.json`, aggregate it into `summary.finish_reason_counts` (with an explicit missing-reason count) and surface the `length` count in the human-readable summary plus the per-slot console summary, so the N=2/N=3/N=4 slot sweep can report the required `finish_reason=length` metric instead of "not recorded".

## Problem statement

The slot-count sweep's acceptance criteria require a `finish_reason=length` count (a smaller per-slot context at N=3/N=4 is expected to truncate more responses), but `proxy/benchmarks/slot_benchmark.py` records no completion reason per request — a `slot_<N>.json` request row carries only `request_index/status/total_duration_seconds/time_to_first_token_seconds/prompt_tokens/completion_tokens/tokens_per_second/resolved_model/error`. The value cannot be recovered post hoc either, because `restart_services()` truncates `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log` during the restore restart, so the 2026-10-23 sweep had to record the metric as **not recorded**.

## Users

- **Producer / capacity owner** deciding `session_slot_pool_size` (keep N=2 vs move to N=3/N=4): needs the truncation count next to TTFT/decode/queue metrics to judge the per-slot-context trade-off.
  - *As a capacity owner, I want the number of truncated (`finish_reason=length`) responses per slot count so I can weigh added decode concurrency against smaller per-slot context.*
- **Benchmark operator** re-running the sweep: wants the metric in the artefacts already produced by the run, with no extra log-parsing step and no dependence on proxy logs surviving the run.
  - *As the operator, I want `summary.finish_reason_counts` in `slot_<N>.json` so the sweep evidence table can be filled in from committed artefacts alone.*

## Existing state

- `proxy/benchmarks/slot_benchmark.py:1045` `send_request()` posts a **non-streaming** chat completion (`"stream": False`, line ~1071) and builds `RequestResult` from `usage` + `X-Resolved-Model`; the response body's `choices[0].finish_reason` is read nowhere.
- `RequestResult` (line ~541) and `SlotRunResult.summary()` (line ~603) are the two places that shape `slot_<N>.json` request rows and the per-run summary.
- `generate_report()` (line ~1414) writes `slot_benchmark_report.json` + `slot_benchmark_summary.txt`; `main()` (line ~1964) prints a per-slot inline summary.
- An in-repo precedent for the exact key name and rendering exists: `scripts/slot_history_extract.py` builds `finish_reason_counts: dict[str, int]` from `Stream finished: … reason=<x>` log lines and renders "Stream finish reasons: …".
- The gap is already documented and linked: `docs/slot-count-reevaluation-LP-0MVGCQ3QN009HRE8.md` lines 232, 289–290, 365 record `finish_reason=length` as "not recorded (harness gap, LP-0MVLHNJ3W007T319)".
- Tests live in `proxy/tests/test_slot_benchmark.py` (report/aggregation/CLI only; no test covers `send_request`).

## Desired change

1. Capture the reason per request in `send_request()` from the non-streaming body (`data["choices"][0].get("finish_reason")`), store it on `RequestResult` as `finish_reason: str | None` (**appended last**, so existing positional constructions stay valid), and emit it in `to_dict()`.
2. Aggregate in `SlotRunResult.summary()`: `finish_reason_counts: dict[str, int]` over completed requests, plus an explicit count of completed requests that reported no reason (absent/nullable reason reported rather than silently omitted, matching the `contention.unavailable` convention already used in this module).
3. Render it: a dedicated finish-reason block in `slot_benchmark_summary.txt` (per slot count: each reason's count, the `length` count, and the missing count) and the same information in the per-slot inline console summary. The existing main table columns stay unchanged.
4. Document the new per-request key and summary field in `proxy/benchmarks/README.md` with a `python -c` inspection snippet (mirroring the existing contention-metrics section).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every `slot_<N>.json` request row carries `finish_reason`, taken from the non-streaming response body's `choices[0].finish_reason`, and `null` when the request errored (non-200/exception) or the provider returned no reason — verified by unit tests that stub the HTTP response.
2. `summary.finish_reason_counts` (present in `slot_<N>.json`, in `slot_benchmark_report.json` `runs[].summary`, and in the in-memory `SlotRunResult.summary()`) maps each observed reason to its count over completed requests, so a truncation count is readable directly as `summary.finish_reason_counts["length"]`, and completed requests with no recorded reason are counted explicitly (not dropped).
3. `slot_benchmark_summary.txt` contains a finish-reason section reporting, per slot count, each reason's count including `length` and the missing-reason count (with `--`/explicit wording when no run recorded any), and the per-slot inline console summary prints the same finish-reason line — both asserted by tests reading the generated artefacts.
4. `proxy/benchmarks/README.md` documents the new per-request `finish_reason` key, the `summary.finish_reason_counts` field and the missing-reason count, including a runnable `python -c` snippet that prints the per-slot reason counts from `slot_benchmark_report.json`.
5. `proxy/tests/test_slot_benchmark.py` gains tests covering: `send_request` capture of a present reason, a missing/null reason (counted as missing), an error request (`finish_reason` is `null`), mixed-reason aggregation in `summary()`, and the summary-file/console rendering — and the full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **No streaming capture path is required.** The harness only issues non-streaming requests (`stream: False`); the streaming variant named in the seed description does not exist in this file. Adding a streaming mode is out of scope (see Assumptions).
- **Backwards compatibility of the artefacts and dataclass:** `RequestResult` is constructed positionally in existing tests and `summary` keys are consumed by `compare_results.py`-style delta comparisons — append the new field last with a default and do not rename/remove existing summary keys or main-table columns.
- **No new production instrumentation, no proxy changes** — the metric comes from the benchmark's own HTTP responses.
- **Do not backfill historical runs.** `proxy/benchmarks/results/slot_sweep_2_3_4_20261023/` cannot be repaired (the restore restart cleared the proxy log); `docs/slot-count-reevaluation-LP-0MVGCQ3QN009HRE8.md` is a historical record and stays as-is (it already links this item as the gap).
- Marker for "no reason recorded" must be distinguishable from reason `"stop"`/`"length"` — do not conflate absent with a fabricated default.
- Restyling/renumbering the existing human-readable report sections is out of scope (only additive changes plus the one console line).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption — non-streaming only:** `send_request()` fixes `stream: False`; the non-streaming `choices[0].finish_reason` is the correct capture point. If a streaming harness is added later, a follow-up item must extend the capture to the last streamed chunk.
- **Assumption — key naming:** `finish_reason_counts` is reused verbatim from `scripts/slot_history_extract.py` so slot evidence tables and extract reports read consistently.
- **Assumption — absence is reported, not guessed:** completed requests with no `finish_reason` are counted separately; the sweep reading rule (only meaningful for locally served requests) is documented rather than enforced.
- **Risk — misleading `length` counts under remote fallback:** a remote provider may report `stop` for a response the local slot would have truncated, so `finish_reason_counts` must be read together with the existing `contention.local_stream_share` (and per-request `resolved_model`). *Mitigation:* AC4 documentation states this reading rule; no per-provider cross-tab is added (scope control).
- **Risk — artefact consumers:** a renamed/removed summary key or a widened main table could break delta comparisons in existing result notes. *Mitigation:* additive-only change (new field appended, new section, existing columns untouched).
- **Risk — scope creep:** per-provider `length` cross-tabs, streaming capture, historical backfill and a proxy-side `finish_reason` metric are all plausible follow-ons. *Mitigation:* they are explicitly out of scope here and should be recorded as linked items if wanted, not folded in.
- **Risk — the metric alone does not unblock the sweep:** the 2026-10-23 runs were also INVALID on local concurrency (`LP-0MVLHNEDO008FTBH`), so this item removes one blocker but does not by itself make the sweep decision-ready.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/tests/test_slot_benchmark.py` — Needs new tests for capture (stubbed `httpx` response), absence/error handling, aggregation and rendering.
- `proxy/benchmarks/README.md` — Needs documentation of the new per-request key, summary field, reading rule (pair with `local_stream_share`) and an inspection snippet.

As an operator, I want local prompt-eval (prefill) throughput increased so that
large cold prompts become cheap enough to serve locally, unlocking real local
utilisation instead of diverting work to paid remote providers.

## GATING PRECONDITION — do not start before this is met

**This item must only be executed once we have had a successful night of local
LLM consumption, meaning >60% GPU utilisation across a full night.** Until
local actually carries sustained work (>60% local busy), tuning prefill
throughput is premature: there is no sustained workload to measure against and
no evidence that prefill latency — rather than routing policy — is the binding
constraint. Verify the gate with the `proxy-usage-analysis` report's
`## Local model utilization` section for a night window (e.g. 22:00-07:00):
it must show busy >= 60%. Record that evidence in a comment on this item
before starting work; if the gate is not met, leave the item blocked.

## Why (current evidence, for context once the gate is met)

- Prompt-eval speed (llama-server eval timing, Qwen3, fast bucket): median
  **90.7 tok/s**, p90 316.7, p10 24.9 (532 samples, 24h window
  2026-10-23 10:52 -> 2026-10-24 10:52).
- Per-stream prefill (dispatch -> first byte): p50 4.4s, p90 35.3s, max 73.7s.
- `local_prefill_deadline_seconds: 90` — a slow prefill can be cancelled, and
  prior incidents show cancelled prefills re-dispatching identical prompts
  (the prefill-thrash cooldown exists because of this).
- The prefill-ETA admission guard refused **478** local admissions in the
  window on projected prefill cost, and only **34** requests were admitted by
  the idle override despite local being idle 89.8% of the time.
- Current llama-server launch flags (Qwen3 child):
  `--ctx-size 262144 --parallel 2 --batch-size 8192 --ubatch-size 1024
  --cache-ram 40960 --cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v q8_0
  --swa-checkpoints 32 --no-mmap -ngl 80 --threads 8`.

- AC0 (GATE): A comment on this item records the measured >60% GPU utilisation

  idle 97.8 %).

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want the A/B benchmark harness to produce valid measurements
in the **40-80k-token** band, because that is the band that produces the
multi-minute local first-byte tail and the only band in which a micro-batch
change can still help.

## Why

`docs/dev/ubatch-ab-2026-10-22.md` (LP-0MVIQ0FSX006HQOS) measured 8.9k / 17.9k
/ 26.8k prompts, found the ubatch 1024->2048 win confined to ~18k (memory
bandwidth bound above), and closed with: *"If this is revisited: measure at
40k-80k tokens"*. The parent item is that revisit, so the harness must be
trustworthy at that size first. Today `build_prompt()` targets ~4 chars/token
without reporting llama-server's real `prompt_tokens`, `--sizes` is free-form,
and a single 80k prefill can take minutes under GPU contention.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: The harness records llama-server's reported `prompt_tokens` per sample
  and fails loudly when the delivered size deviates from the requested size by
  more than 10 %, so a mis-sized prompt cannot silently invalidate a bin.
- AC2: An end-to-end run at `--sizes 40960,61440,81920 --reps 3` produces a
  JSON result with per-size p50/p90 and the 20k+ headline aggregate within a
  documented time budget and timeout.
- AC3: Offline unit tests cover prompt sizing/token accounting, percentile
  aggregation, size-deviation rejection and argument validation - no live
  server required.
- AC4: `docs/dev/` records the band methodology and validity guards: unique
  prompt text per repetition, `cache_prompt: false`, the TTS/GPU-contention
  noise rule, and minimum reps.
- AC5: Full suite green via the test skill.

**Key Files:**
- `scripts/ubatch_ab_benchmark.py` - the A/B harness
- `tests/test_ubatch_ab_benchmark.py` - offline harness tests
- `docs/dev/ubatch-ab-2026-10-22.md` - prior experiment record to extend

## Implementation sketch (test-first)

1. Extend the offline tests for the new validations.
2. Report and validate actual `prompt_tokens`; fail fast on a mis-sized bin.
3. Add a documented default band (`40960,61440,81920`) and a per-size timeout
   policy.
4. Record the methodology in `docs/dev/`.

## Dependencies

- Verify sustained local utilisation gate.
- Experiment: 1 slot at 262K ctx vs 2 slots at 131K ctx (LP-0MVMHNUXW0061FGN) -
  a 40-80k prompt must fit the per-slot context.

## Out of scope

Changing llama-server flags, routing or admission policy.

## Problem

`proxy/proxy/handlers.py:489` carries a `# noqa` comment whose text is prose
rather than a comma-separated code list, so ruff cannot parse it as a
suppression. Every `ruff check` run in this repo — repo-wide or file-scoped —
prints a warning to stderr:

```
$ ruff check --select I001 proxy/proxy/handlers.py
warning: Invalid `# noqa` directive on proxy/proxy/handlers.py:489: expected a
comma-separated list of codes (e.g. `# noqa: F401, F841`).
All checks passed!
```

Current source:

```python
    import os  # noqa: local import for config access
```

## Why it matters

- The comment gives no suppression at all: whatever it was intended to silence
  (`F401`? a local-import / `PLC0415` style rule?) is either already allowed by
  `.ruff.toml` or silently expressed as prose — so the intent is unrecoverable
  from the code.
- It makes every lint invocation in this repository noisy, which trains readers
  and agents to ignore ruff's warning channel — the exact channel that would
  surface a genuinely broken suppression.
- It was noted as a known-but-out-of-scope side observation while clearing the
  `I001` findings of epic `LP-0MVLK5H04003FZJS` (see
  `LP-0MVKE61H9001WPAQ` for the earlier sighting).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — warning cleared:** `python3 -m ruff check proxy/proxy/handlers.py`
      produces no `Invalid \`noqa\` directive` warning and still reports
      `All checks passed!` (command + output captured on the work item).
- [ ] **AC2 — intent preserved:** the reason for the directive is expressed
      either as a valid code list (e.g. `# noqa: PLC0415`) that matches the
      rule actually triggered, or as a plain explanatory comment with no
      `noqa` prefix. Determined by removing the directive and re-running ruff
      on the file to see which rule (if any) fires; recorded in the closure
      comment.
- [ ] **AC3 — no blanket suppression:** `.ruff.toml` gains no new
      `per-file-ignores`/global `ignore` entry for `proxy/proxy/handlers.py`,
      so genuine future findings remain detectable (`git diff --stat` on
      `.ruff.toml` empty for this item).
- [ ] **AC4 — no behaviour change:** the change is comment-only; the
      `import os` statement itself is untouched, so runtime behaviour is
      identical.
- [ ] **AC5 — full suite green:** validation runs through the test skill
      (`/skill:test`, changed scope at the implement gate, full suite at the
      dev-push gate) — no ad-hoc `pytest`.

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/handlers.py` — line 489 holds the invalid directive
  (`import os  # noqa: local import for config access`).
- `.ruff.toml` — **must remain unchanged**; no suppression may be added.

## Provenance

Discovered from: `LP-0MVLK5H04003FZJS` (Quality Improvement - Refactoring epic) while
closing child `LP-0MVMLII27004JVII` — that item verified
`ruff check --select I001 .` clean at HEAD `9db15857` and this stray `# noqa`
warning was the only remaining lint-channel noise observed. Earlier sighting
recorded in `LP-0MVKE61H9001WPAQ`. Not blocking that epic: the epic tracks
`I001` findings, and this is a distinct (pre-existing) hygiene defect.

## Problem

The dev-push full-suite gate (`.githooks/pre-push`) may not validate the commit
actually being pushed when `implement.py finish` recovers from a
non-fast-forward rejection.

Observed while finishing LP-0MVQ239VQ001RXZ0 (2026-10-28 ~04:45Z):

1. First push attempt from the worktree was rejected non-fast-forward.
2. `_recover_non_fast_forward_push()` rebased onto `origin/dev` and retried with
   `git_push_to_dev(repo_root, ...)` — i.e. **`cwd` = the main checkout**, not
   the worktree (implement.py:4737). The pre-push hook therefore runs
   `run_tests.py --scope full --project-root <main-checkout>`, which tests the
   **main checkout's working tree** (HEAD `75aff4f0` at the time), not the
   rebased commit (`722892e1`) being pushed. It passed instantly on a cache
   entry for that unrelated tree.
3. The whole finish (including both push attempts) took ~68 s, far below the
   ~356–386 s a cold full-suite run costs. No cached full-suite entry existed
   for the pushed tree at that point, so the first attempt's hook run cannot
   have executed the suite either. That part is unexplained and worth
   instrumenting (hook stderr is swallowed by `subprocess.PIPE` unless the push
   fails).

Net effect: a dev push can land without the full suite ever having run against
the pushed tree. Verified after the fact by running the suite in a detached
worktree at `722892e1`: 5819 passed, 16 skipped, 2 xfailed (green), and the
cache entry was mirrored into `.worklog/cache/47939ae8ae101342b387f2052425286a`.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A dev push through `implement.py finish` provably runs the full-suite gate
   against the **pushed commit's tree** (assert on the runner's git state /
   `--project-root` in the hook, e.g. by logging the resolved root and HEAD).
2. The non-fast-forward retry path either pushes from the worktree (so the hook
   validates the rebased commit) or passes the pushed tree explicitly to the
   gate; the main checkout's working tree is never the subject of the gate.
3. Hook/push stderr is surfaced in the `implement.py finish` log (at least at
   DEBUG/INFO) so "the gate ran and hit a cache" is distinguishable from "the
   gate never ran".
4. A regression test covers the retry path's gate root (unit test around
   `_recover_non_fast_forward_push` / `git_push_to_dev` cwd choice).

## Evidence

- `implement.py:4737` — retry push uses `repo_root` as cwd.
- Finish log for LP-0MVQ239VQ001RXZ0: `Push failed (non-fast-forward); attempting rebase and retry` → `Push to dev succeeded` within ~10 s of the commit.
- Post-hoc verification run at `722892e1`: 5819 passed, 16 skipped, 2 xfailed.
